T: Ring the bells. Ring the dinner bell.
D: A kind bell-ringer hidden in Notre Dame sneaks out to the Festival of Fools in Paris.
P: Serve the snacks when Quasimodo sneaks down to the Festival of Fools.
S: the Festival of Fools in the square
Thin crêpe batter rested an hour, cooked in a buttered pan, folded with ham and gruyère, or with sugar and lemon.
Hugo, Victor and Laverne's croque bites
the three gargoyles cheering Quasimodo on

Little ham and gruyère toasties smothered in béchamel and grilled until bubbling and blistered, cut into bites with cornichons. Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp plain flour, then whisk in 200ml milk and cook until thick, and season with nutmeg. Spread 4 slices of bread with Dijon mustard, top with 150g ham and 80g grated gruyère, and close with 4 more slices. Toast in a buttered pan for 2 minutes a side. Spread the tops with béchamel, scatter with 60g more gruyère and grill until bubbling. Cut into 6 bites each.
the busy Paris market below the cathedral
Baguette slices toasted with olive oil, topped with brie and fig jam, or with tomato and basil.
M: Bell tower beef and mushroom braise

Beef chuck braised slow with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions in a rich dark stock until spoon tender, served over buttery mash. Brown 150g diced bacon, then brown 1.2kg diced beef chuck in batches. Add 12 peeled baby onions and 300g mushrooms and colour lightly. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour and 2 tbsp tomato paste, then add 750ml beef stock, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, thyme and 2 bay leaves. Cover and simmer gently for 3 hours. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and warm milk.

Chicken thighs braised with garlic, green olives, lemon and herbs until tender and saucy, with crusty bread to mop it all up. Season 1kg chicken thighs and brown skin side down in olive oil for 6 minutes, then turn. Add 10 whole peeled garlic cloves, 100g green olives, 1 sliced lemon, thyme and 2 bay leaves. Pour in 300ml chicken stock, cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes, then uncover and bubble for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens. Scatter with parsley and serve with crusty bread.
W: the great cathedral of Notre Dame
Madeleine batter of butter, eggs, sugar and lemon zest rested an hour, baked in shell tins at 200C for 10 minutes.
K: Esmeralda and her goat Djali in the Paris square

French-style sirop à l'eau: homemade pomegranate grenadine and lime poured into iced soda so it sinks red, stirred at the table. Simmer 250ml pomegranate juice with 100g caster sugar for 10 minutes until slightly syrupy, add a squeeze of lemon and cool. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice and add the juice of a quarter lime to each. Top with soda water, then slowly pour 3 tbsp of the grenadine down the side of each glass so it settles at the bottom. Serve with a spoon to stir.

s.note: the Festival of Fools in the square
s.how: Whisk 150g flour, 2 eggs and 375ml milk and rest an hour. Cook thin crepes in a buttered pan. Fill half with ham and gruyere and fold, warming until melted. Sprinkle the rest with sugar and lemon juice and fold into quarters.

s.note: the busy Paris market below the cathedral
s.how: Slice a baguette, brush with olive oil and toast. Top half with brie and a spoon of fig jam. Top the rest with chopped tomato, torn basil and salt. Lay them out like a stall at the Paris market below the bell tower.

w.note: the great cathedral of Notre Dame
w.how: Melt 100g butter and cool. Whisk 2 eggs with 100g sugar and lemon zest until thick, then fold in 100g flour and the butter. Rest for an hour. Spoon into greased shell tins and bake at 200C for 10 minutes. Dust with icing sugar.
